goals.title: Simulation-first robot factory and local-AI research foundation
goals.purpose: Design a long-term autonomous fabrication workcell. Start with deterministic simulations, budget-constrained 3D-print experiments and evaluated local-AI training data before any large physical hardware purchases or motion control.
acceptance: Reproducible pure-Python geometry/kinematics tests pass without physical devices.
Initial 3D-print coupons are generated and tested only on hardware physically available; measured results must be recorded, never fabricated.
Local-AI dataset provenance, baselines, evaluation split and model limitations are documented before training.
Separate simulation, model planning, safety controller and physical device interfaces; no unapproved actuation.
An isolated AIBridge worker is registered and verified before worker_enabled is switched to 1 or any runtime task is queued.
All future physical manufacturing must use validated stations, guards and independently enforced emergency stops.

milestones.title: Repository architecture, Guides, deterministic simulation baseline and CI
milestones.evidence: 2026-10-31: PR #1 squash-merged to main commit 57662a6356e7366499caff54a92f8df4f2b47ae7. GitHub Actions PR run 41172803690 PASS across Ubuntu/Windows Python 3.10/3.12 (4/4 jobs; 10 deterministic unittest cases/job). This proves pure offline Python baseline only. Dedicated worker registration, Windows owner-machine result, printer calibration, local model training and robot control remain unverified. Keep bridgeTask.worker_enabled=0 until Manager identity/CDP/checkout validated.
